**Finding submitted: T4C — deviation (high).**

- **What the document does:** Section 11.1 commits Corio to an initial five-year term with automatic one-year renewals; Section 11.2 permits termination only for uncured material breach or insolvency. No convenience right exists for either party anywhere in the Agreement (the p0050 acceptance-test exit and p0079 warranty exit are conditional remedies, not convenience rights).
- **Why it fails fallback:** The fallback requires a Customer convenience right on 60–90 days' notice; here Corio has none at all in a multi-year committed term, which is the walk-away scenario in the playbook.
- **Not double-flagged:** The 30-day non-renewal notice in 11.1 is natural-term non-renewal (RENEWAL), not a Vendor mid-term convenience right.
- **Cure (preferred, one insertion as new 11.4):** Corio convenience termination on 30 days' written notice, pro rata refund of prepaid fees, and an express bar on Commerce One convenience termination during the initial or renewal terms. No partial-termination or Order Form language was added, since this contract has no Order Form structure.
